sources.title: University of Mumbai, History of Medieval India (1000-1526 CE), pp.11-12
sources.note: Original institutional PDF indexed sections1.4.7.1 and1.4.7.2 read: Chaulukya rivalry, Chauhan expansion, Gahadavala hostility, Tarain1191/1192. Problematic reign dates1178-1193 not adopted. Replaces incomplete SATHEE transcription of NCERT chapter, which omits Warfare for Wealth.

sources.title: F. Kielhorn, The Chahamanas of Naddula, Epigraphia Indica IX, p.62
sources.note: Indexed primary scholarly edition read, opening comparison of Shakambhari genealogies: Harsha VS1030/973 and Bijolia VS1226/1170. Only chronology and changing genealogical scope used. Unstable early identifications of Nagavaloka/Nagabhata are excluded.

sources.title: Elizabeth A. Cecil, Mapping the Pasupata Landscape, chapter 3 (2020)
sources.note: Publisher chapter and whole-book indexed text checked; direct extraction failed. Chapter 3 pp.117-122, especially translations of Harsha inscription verses 33-43. Reproducible queries: site:brill.com "Bhāvadyota" "well"; "Śākambharī" "viṃśopaka"; "Caṇḍaśiva" "Vīrabhadra". Entire book and chapter treated as one source, not multiplied URL allowance.

sources.title: Ram Sharma, Three Jinmata Temple Inscriptions of Imperial Chahamana Dynasty, Epigraphia Indica XLII, pp.60-64
sources.note: Official PDF downloaded and relevant pages visually inspected: printed 60/PDF index96, 61/index99, 62/index100, 63/index103. Two 1140 pillar inscriptions, Sanskrit/Nagari, renovation by Udayaraja sons Alhana and Delhana. A third record dated 1174 June10 identifies Alhana and architect Kaladharadeva. Writing excerpt from B lines11-12, p.62, with normalized Roman transliteration; A line6 provides parallel.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica V, p.104: Sanskrit closing formula and translation
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly edition, inscription B line5 and closing English translation: Mangalam maha-srih / Bliss! Great prosperity! Used only to verify the conventional Sanskrit blessing translation, not to identify the Chola inscription as a Chahamana record.

sources.title: Rajasthan Foundation, Ajmer district guide: Ana Sagar Lake
sources.note: Official indexed Ana Sagar and Anasagar Baradari sections read. Arnoraja lake dated 1135-1150; later Mughal gardens and pavilions separated. No claims about modern water purity, universal household access or medieval baths inferred.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Bharat SHRI: Harakeli-nataka inscription from Ajmer
sources.note: Direct official gallery read, entry HARIKELI-NATAKA OF VIGRAHARAJADEVA FROM AJMER. Date VS1210/22 November1153, Sanskrit and Prakrit/Nagari, fifth act conversation, engraver Bhaskara. Entry cites Indian Antiquary XX, p.201ff.

sources.title: Har Bilas Sarda, Ajmer: Historical and Descriptive, p.77
sources.note: Official digitized book downloaded; title/contents visually inspected and indexed p.77 Inscriptions read. Six basalt tablets discovered in courtyard in1875-76, four with play fragments including Somadeva. Only this concrete documentary account used, not the book’s expansive military claims or communal judgments.

sources.title: Ministry of Tourism, Incredible India: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra
sources.note: Full original indexed text read after direct timeout: site associated with Vigraharaja IV Sanskrit college, reused Hindu/Jain temple material in mosque, Quranic decoration and later architecture. Treats two-and-a-half-day building as legend; no literal construction duration adopted.

sources.title: Cynthia Talbot, The Last Hindu Emperor: Prithviraj Chauhan and the Indian Past (Cambridge University Press)
sources.note: Original publisher full indexed description and contents read; 800 years of changing narratives and modern last-Hindu-emperor epithet. No later heroic tale presented as contemporary biography.

sources.title: Cynthia Talbot, Turks, Warriors, and Conquerors, Oxford Handbook of the Mughal World (2020)
sources.note: Original scholarly abstract read through index after direct redirect failure: Prithviraj of Ajmer defeated by Muhammad of Ghur1192, Hammir Chauhan of Ranthambhor defeated by Ala al-Din Khalji1301; later heroic narratives. No direct succession or one uninterrupted empire asserted.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Shakambhari/Ajmer Chahamana ruling line; no additional aliases or absorption of Nadol, Jalor or Ranthambhor records.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: identity.json decodes six polygons from world-600 through world-1100, all broadly northern Rajasthan/Delhi belt. Southern bounds near26.544N exclude Ajmer centre near26.45N. Public opening states exclusion and approximate chronology; no map repair claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 973 and1170 genealogical witnesses; detailed records1140,1153,1174;1192 conquest and later1301 branch history. Period973 begins source-visible documentary coverage, not dynastic foundation. Imported600 start is not confirmed as an imperial founding year.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No source-supported household medical or toilet practice located in this bounded research. Water, gardening, cattle, craft families, donor brothers and literary learning provide concrete ordinary-life evidence without inventing universal customs.
